cold_sentence: On cold questions C4 reduced median TTFT by 1.12 s (CI 0.66 to 1.49), because it prefills fewer tokens (Fig.~\ref{fig:ttft}).
confound: Decode speed does not depend on the prompt, so it serves as a health indicator for the host. The passes C2 Uniform LLMLingua-2, C5 Sieve, no ledger, C6 8k context, C4 $-$verifier ran at a median decode speed below 75\% of C0's 26.8 tok/s because of host memory pressure (calls flagged as degraded: C2 18, C5 11, C6 35, C4 16). Their absolute latencies are inflated and are not used for latency comparisons; their token and accuracy results are unaffected. C0 and C4 ran at matching decode speeds (26.8 and 28.9 tok/s).
abl_text: Removing the verifier changed accuracy from 0.911 to 0.850 while saving 32.6\% of tokens instead of 31.0\%; with the verifier, C4 re-inflated 270 segment compressions. Removing the ledger lowered mean prefix reuse from 45\% to 17\% and raised prefill per conversation from 1,981 to 3,064 tokens. The classifier trained on heuristic labels reached 0.917 and the classifier restricted to the six core features 0.939, against 0.911 for C4; their paired intervals overlap with C4's. Prefetching never triggered in any condition, so the $-$prefetch variant sent the same prompts as C4.
be_text:
Fig.~\ref{fig:be} sweeps the probability $p$ that a question needs a large archived document that C4 externalizes (8 cold conversations per point). Mean net time per question was 4.47 s for C4 and 8.51 s for C0 at $p=0$, and 7.63 s and 9.42 s at $p=1$, where C4 expanded on 75\% of questions. The curves did not cross in the swept range: in this setting externalization paid off even when every question needed the document, because C0's prompt overflowed the window and was prefilled in full on every call. Accuracy at $p=1$ was 0.88 for C4 and 0.50 for C0.
\begin{figure}[t]\centering\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{fig_breakeven.pdf}\caption{Externalization break-even: mean net time per question (Sieve CPU time plus model time, including tool round trips) as the probability that a question needs the externalized document grows.}\label{fig:be}\end{figure}
fam_text: C4 was above C0 in families B, C, E, F, G and below it in D, J, K.
supported: Sieve reduced prompt tokens by 31.0\% with an interval that excludes zero, improved accuracy on prompts that overflowed the window (+36.2 pp), lowered median cold TTFT by 1.12 s; its overall accuracy change is not statistically distinguishable from zero. The cache test and the C4--C5 comparison support the ledger as the mechanism that keeps compression compatible with prefix caching.
losses: On short prompts (under about 1,500 tokens) C4 saved 15.8\% of tokens and reached accuracy 0.94 against 1.00 for C0. Families D, J, K lost accuracy under C4. On warm questions the raw prompt's prefix is already cached, so latency differences there are small (0.33 s vs.\ 0.46 s median). C4 hard-truncated 15 prompts that remained over budget after compression and externalization.
prefetch_sentence: Prefetching never triggered at the 0.75 similarity threshold, so the $-$prefetch ablation sent the same content as C4 and differs only in timing.
abstract: Local large language models share one fixed context window between the prompt and the answer, and long conversations waste it on verbose, repeated and stale text. Prompt compression reduces tokens but rewrites the prefix, which defeats the key-value (KV) prefix cache that local servers rely on. This paper presents Sieve, a middleware that splits each request into segments and routes every segment to one of three lanes: COMPRESS (LLMLingua-2 pruning at a per-segment ratio, checked by a rule-based verifier of facts and their context), CACHE (kept byte-identical so the KV prefix is reused) or EXTERNALIZE (replaced by a deterministic stub that the model can expand through a tool call). Hard rules run first, a cost-sensitive gradient-boosting classifier routes the rest, and a per-session ledger replays emitted strings so compression does not invalidate the cached prefix. On 180 ground-truth questions from 76 synthetic conversations with invented entities, run on Qwen3-14B through Ollama with a 4096-token window, Sieve reduced prompt tokens by 31.0\% (95\% CI 27.8--34.0\%) and raised mean output headroom from 1,349 to 2,393 tokens. Its accuracy change of +5.0 percentage points (CI -0.6 to +11.1) is not statistically distinguishable from zero, while on prompts that overflowed the window accuracy rose by 36.2 points (CI +19.1 to +53.2). Median time to first token on cold questions fell by 1.12 s. A controlled test shows that re-compressing a prefix reduces prefill reuse from 95\% to 2\%, and that sending the memoized compressed string restores it to 89\%. Code, logs and traces are public.
